title: Find a panel's query and data source

blocks.content: Explore a panel to see where its data comes from: the data source, the query, and the result format.

blocks.title: Find the query and its data source

blocks.content: Find the **Base Query (A) - Total CPU Usage** panel.

steps.reftarget: div[data-viz-panel-key='panel-3'] button[data-testid='data-testid Panel menu Base Query (A) - Total CPU Usage']
steps.description: Click here to open the panel menu.
Click Edit to open the panel editor.

blocks.content: Notice the data source for query **A**. It's a Prometheus data source, so Grafana sends this query to Prometheus.
This is the query. A data source holds far more data than one panel needs, and the query returns just the data this visualization needs.

Below the query, the options row shows **Format: Time series**. Format determines how the result is interpreted in the panel, so it must suit the visualization: the Table format, for example, works only in a table. A stat or gauge can still take a time series result by reducing it to one value.

blocks.reftarget: [data-testid='data-testid Standard options Unit field property editor']
blocks.content: Under **Standard options**, the panel's **Unit** is set to **core**, the unit its values are measured in.

steps.description: Click Back to return to the dashboard.

steps.reftarget: button[data-testid='data-testid Exit edit mode button'], button[data-testid='data-testid Edit dashboard button']
steps.description: The dashboard is still in edit mode. Click Exit edit.

blocks.content: If Grafana asks about unsaved changes, select **Discard**. Nothing needed saving.
